sourceDecisionQuestions.question: The current source objective literally says lead a complete roofing day in Spanish. The archived French objective changes the language to French, but English is the target for this pair. Keep exact source provenance and obtain a qualified English-learning capstone objective before learner use.

Tear-off and closeout are trade process terms; the source has an install/instalación part-of-speech mismatch, while archived poser is a verb for a term labeled instalación. Confirm English target, French support and dictionary senses, and whether the tear-off/install sequence is job-specific rather than universal.

Underlayment, flashing, deck and tarp require roof-system/product scope; the Reader says the lead checks each step. Archived platelage, sous-couche and solin may be conditional but cannot select a specific assembly or inspection approval.

The source tie-off command mentions a harness without an approved anchor, fall-clearance or site system. Archived attachez-vous is broader and can obscure the tie-off requirement. Hold for qualified fall-protection and French terminology review.

The source storm warning is followed by a conditional order to stop and descend if weather changes, then an unfinished-section tarp action. Archived Reader 7 changes its English anchor by adding 'once conditions allow safe work under the approved plan'; preserve the current source exact text and hold the timing, weather stop and tarp access sequence for qualified safety/source review.

Punch list/closeout and the final roof walk must remain open-item and day-end scene meanings, not unconditional roof access or completion certification. Archived speaking adds safety-plan and temporary-cover assertions beyond the source roleplay objective.
